title: Large-coin daily cross-sectional momentum: hold the top-4 of nine pairs by prior UTC-day return for 23 hours
ex_ante_rule: Chart 1h, closed bars only, all times UTC. Signal at the close of bar t, order filled at the open of bar t+1. Long only, spot, one position per traded pair, whole allowed balance, no pyramiding, no take-profit, no sizing hooks. Universe: the nine pairs BTC/USDT, ETH/USDT, BNB/USDT, XRP/USDT, ADA/USDT, LTC/USDT, LINK/USDT, DOGE/USDT, SOL/USDT; every pair other than the traded one is loaded as an informative 1h pair (merge_informative_pair, closed bars, aligned on the same candle timestamp). RANKING (once per day): at the close of the 23:00 UTC bar of day d-1, for each of the nine pairs compute R = close(23:00 bar of day d-1) / close(23:00 bar of day d-2) - 1 (the 24-bar return). A pair is dropped from that day's ranking if any of its 25 hourly closes from the 23:00 bar of d-2 through the 23:00 bar of d-1 is missing. Rank the remaining pairs by R, highest first; exact ties are broken by pair name in ascending alphabetical order (the alphabetically earlier name ranks higher). ENTRY: the entry signal is raised only on the 23:00 UTC bar, and only if the traded pair is in the ranking and its rank is 1, 2, 3 or 4 (top 4); the order fills at the open of the 00:00 UTC bar of day d. No entry signal on any other bar. EXIT: time exit; exit signal at the close of the 22:00 UTC bar of day d, filled at the open of the 23:00 UTC bar (every trade lasts 23 hours, under 24 hours). STOP-LOSS: one fixed 5% below the entry price, the engine's native intrabar stop (triggers as soon as price touches it). After a stop-out, no re-entry until the next daily decision at the 23:00 bar. Each day is a fresh decision; a pair in the top 4 on consecutive days is closed at 23:00 and re-bought at 00:00 (no carry-over). No trend filter, no cooldown other than the above, no other conditions. Warm-up: 50 bars (longest lookback is 25 closes / 24-bar return; no recursive indicators; startup_candle_count = 50 covers informative alignment).
rationale: Zaremba et al. (IRFA 2021) find that across 3,600+ coins the previous day's return reverses, mainly as compensation for illiquidity, but that the handful of largest and most tradeable coins show daily momentum instead. Begusic and Kostanjcar (arXiv 1904.00890) report strong momentum among the most liquid coins and link it to investor herding. All nine lab pairs are in that large, liquid group. Who gives the money away: attention-limited and late buyers who chase yesterday's leaders during the next day, and the gradual spread of news and flows across the big coins, which lifts the relative winners into the following day. Trade count: a pair is in the top 4 of 9 on about 4/9 of days, so roughly 160 trades per year per pair, inside the 150-500 target. Move per trade: each trade holds a large alt for 23 hours, and these coins typically move 2-5% a day, so the gross move per trade aims well above the 0.30% base and 0.45% conservative round trip; the edge needed is a small positive drift on a large move. Risk: the 5% native stop caps any single loss; with whole balance per trade, a streak of losses is limited by the daily-move size, not by long holds. Success is judged only by the existing gates (positive net at base and conservative cost, drawdown under 25%, at least 6 of 9 pairs). Parameters are taken as written in the idea, fixed ex ante, no grid.
novelty_vs_tried: First cross-sectional ranking rule over the whole nine-pair universe. H-031 CrossPairCatchUp buys a laggard after a 2-bar jump of two peers (reversal-to-peer, 4h hold); H-047 RelativeStrengthRatioRotation uses a ratio-to-basket breakout over hundreds of bars with SMA exits; H-072 is a residual reversal against one reference; H-015/H-016 TimeSeriesMomentum use each pair's own trend. Here the signal is the pair's rank among nine by the prior UTC-day return, decided once a day at a fixed hour, held for a fixed 23 hours, with no trend filter and no indicator.

sources.title: Up or down? Short-term reversal, momentum, and liquidity effects in cryptocurrency markets (Zaremba, Bilgin, Long, Mercik, Szczygielski, IRFA 78, 2021)
Momentum and liquidity in cryptocurrencies (Begusic, Kostanjcar, arXiv 1904.00890)
